Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
What is the atomic number of Calcium?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
In what year was Sam Altman born?
Sam Altman: Altman attended Stanford University for two years before he dropped out and co-founded Loopt, a smartphone geosocial networking service.
In what year was Bayes' theorem discovered?
Bayes' theorem: The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.
Genetics: Gregor Mendel. Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Which country is Bombardier Challenger 600 series from?
Bombardier Challenger 600 series: Canada. At the end of 1975, Canadair began funding the development of LearStar 600, and then bought the design for a wide-cabin business jet in April 1976.
Who is credited with discovering Hassium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Hassium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Who is credited with discovering HD 209458 b?
HD 209458 b: Michel Mayor. It is sometimes informally called Osiris.
Who is credited with discovering Osmium?
Osmium: Smithson Tennant. Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
One of the very few semiaquatic vipers in the world, which venomous pit viper native to the southeastern United States is often found coiled near slow-moving lakes, streams, and marshes?
Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.

With more than 140 species spread across 16 genera in oceans worldwide, these small forage fish are usually classified as oily fish, and a few South American species live only in fresh water — name this fish?
Anchovy are small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae.
Excavated in Argentina starting in 1989 under paleontologist José Bonaparte, this Late Cretaceous titanosaur weighed as much as 80 tons — which genus of giant sauropod?
Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Developed in Great Britain around the 1830s from breeds like the Talbot Hound, this scent hound — smaller than the similar-looking foxhound — was originally bred to hunt rabbits and hares — name the breed?
Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
This insect order contains both cockroaches and termites — the latter now classified as a specialized, social lineage within the former group — what order is it?
Blattodea is an order of insects that contains cockroaches and termites.

More muscular and aggressive than the females of the species, this uncastrated adult male of Bos taurus has long symbolized power in religious sacrifice and features prominently in ranching and blood sports — which term describes him?
Bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
This Mexican business magnate was ranked the richest person in the world by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, building his fortune through a sprawling conglomerate called Grupo Carso. Who is he?
Carlos Slim (born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.
The principal sterol of all animals, it concentrates in the brain and spinal cord and is essential to every cell membrane — yet too much in the blood spells trouble. What is it?
Cholesterol is the principal sterol of all animals, distributed in body tissues, especially the brain and spinal cord, and in animal fats and oils.
This legless, non-venomous lizard native to Europe is often mistaken for a snake despite having smooth, non-overlapping scales and semi-fossorial burrowing habits — what is it called?
Common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.

Bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba, Argentina, for hunting big game like wild boar and pumas, this large mastiff-type dog breed traces its ancestry partly to a now-extinct fighting dog — name the breed?
Dogo Argentino (plural Dogos Argentinos) is an Argentine breed of large dog of mastiff type.
Born to a mathematician father in Erlangen, this pioneering algebraist proved theorems connecting symmetry to conservation laws in physics — who is she?
Emmy Noether (23 March 1882 - 14 April 1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra.
Despite its name, this highly sociable oceanic dolphin earned its label from a skull resembling the orca's — it can reach 20 feet and even forms mixed pods with bottlenose dolphins. What is it?
False killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) is a species of oceanic dolphin that is the only extant representative of the genus Pseudorca.

This American mechanical engineer and pioneering management consultant wrote a 1909 book that Academy of Management fellows later voted the most influential management book of the entire 20th century — who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor (March 20, 1856 - March 21, 1915) was an American mechanical engineer.
This ancient metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate through ten enzyme-catalyzed reactions in a cell's cytosol, generating ATP along the way. What process is it?
Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway that converts glucose (C6H12O6) into pyruvate and, in most organisms, occurs in the liquid part of cells (the cytosol).
About the size of a closed fist and tucked between the lungs, this four-chambered muscular organ pumps blood throughout the body — name it?
Heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
A colourless, ammonia-scented liquid with formula N2H4, this hazardous compound foams polymers, inflates airbags, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Serving as the continuous analog of a summation, this fundamental calculus operation is used to compute areas, volumes, and displacement from velocity — name the mathematical concept?
Integral is the continuous analog of a sum, and is used to calculate areas, volumes, and their generalizations.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
Named after a 19th-century Russian neuropsychiatrist, which memory disorder features confabulation and amnesia from vitamin B1 deficiency, often following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy?
Korsakoff syndrome (KS) is a disorder of the central nervous system characterized by amnesia, deficits in explicit memory, and confabulation.
One of only five people to win multiple Nobel Prizes, this American chemist and peace activist is the sole person to have received two unshared Nobels — one in Chemistry, one for Peace. Who is he?
Linus Pauling (February 28, 1901 - August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.

This colorless, highly water-soluble inorganic salt forms hydrates holding up to 12 water molecules per unit, and its anhydrous form is industry's main source for producing a lightweight, silvery-white structural metal — which compound is it?
Magnesium chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula MgCl2.
First made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, this synthetic element 101 is named for the father of the periodic table — what is it?
Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.

Caused by a poxvirus spread through direct contact, this viral skin infection produces small raised pink lesions with a distinctive dimple in the center, usually clearing on its own within a year — name the condition?
Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.

Nicknamed for its terrifying rate of tissue destruction, this fast-spreading bacterial infection doesn't actually consume flesh — the bacteria instead release toxins that destroy it — what is this disease called?
Necrotizing fasciitis (NF), also known as flesh-eating disease or flesh-eating bacteria, is an infection that kills the body's soft tissue.

Encompassing 24 genera from baboons to colobus to langurs, this is the largest primate family, having diverged from a separate primate lineage 45 to 55 million years ago before apes split off from it too — which family?
Old World monkey are primates in the family Cercopithecidae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
One of nine essential amino acids we must eat rather than make ourselves, it's found in mammals' milk and acts as a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine — which molecule is it?
Phenylalanine (symbol Phe or F) is an -amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2.

This natural process transfers pollen from a flower's anther to its stigma, enabling fertilization and seed production, carried out by everything from bees and bats to wind and water — what process is it?
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.

This psychiatric state describes an inability to distinguish reality from delusion, marked by symptoms like hallucinations and disorganized thinking, and can stem from conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder — name the state?
Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real.
This inflammatory disease typically develops two to four weeks after a streptococcal throat infection and can damage the heart valves in about half of cases — what is it?
Rheumatic fever (RF) is an inflammatory disease that can involve the heart, joints, skin, and brain.
After dropping out of Stanford and co-founding a startup later sold for over $40 million, this entrepreneur led Y Combinator before taking the helm of a leading AI company — who is he?
Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019.
The smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds, this small, alert hunting dog's name literally translates to 'brushwood dog,' reflecting its original job of flushing game — which breed?
Shiba Inu (Japanese) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.

Meaning 'pore bearer' in Greek, this phylum of sessile, filter-feeding marine invertebrates has tube-like bodies of jelly-like material sandwiched between thin cell layers, letting water circulate through countless pores — name the animal group?
Sponge are primarily marine invertebrates of the animal phylum Porifera (meaning 'pore bearer').

This amniote lineage — one of just two major branches alongside the reptile-and-bird clade — is marked by a single temporal opening behind the eye and gave rise to every mammal alive today — name the group?
Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
This genus of coniferous evergreen in the cypress family includes five species — two native to North America, three to eastern Asia — and is sister to the genus Thujopsis. Name the genus?
Thuja is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
The two major groups of these reptiles, side-necked and hidden-necked, differ in how they pull in the head — and they breathe air despite many living in water. What animal?
Turtle (order Testudines) are reptiles characterized by a special shell developed mainly from their ribs, as well as keratinized toothless beak.

This trailing vine of the gourd family bears a fruit that's botanically a 'pepo' — a hard-rinded berry with no internal divisions — and comes in more than 1,000 varieties, even seedless ones. What is it?
Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.
Adding or subtracting this number leaves any other number unchanged. In mathematical terms it is the additive what, of the integers and the reals?

0 is a number representing an empty quantity. Adding or subtracting 0 to any number leaves that number unchanged; in mathematical terminology 0 is the additive identity of the integers, rational numbers, real numbers and complex numbers.
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.
With the general formula CnH2n+2 and every carbon-carbon bond single, methane is the simplest example of this class of hydrocarbons — what's it called?
Alkane: Type of saturated hydrocarbon compound.
This group of diseases occurs when misfolded proteins accumulate in body tissue, causing fatigue, swelling, and shortness of breath among roughly 36 distinct protein-driven types — what is it?
Amyloidosis: Metabolic disease involving abnormal deposited amyloid proteins.
Usually symptomless until it ruptures — causing sudden, severe abdominal or lower-back pain — this dangerous enlargement of the body's main artery is most common in the abdomen — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm: Excessive enlargement of the human aorta.
Born from acetylsalicylic acid, this everyday drug cools fevers within about 30 minutes and is taken long-term to fend off heart attacks and strokes by quieting platelets — what is it?
A Kenyan economist who met his future wife at the University of Hawaii, this man became the father of a future U.S. president and the subject of that son's 1995 memoir — who is he?
Before becoming TV's most famous bow-tied science educator, this Boeing mechanical engineer invented a hydraulic resonance suppressor tube for 747s, then quit to do sketch comedy. Who is he?

A twin-engine, carrier-capable strike fighter flown by the U.S., Australia, and Kuwait, this larger, more advanced follow-on to an earlier 1980s Navy jet packs an internal 20 mm rotary cannon and can be rigged as an airborne refueling tanker — what is it called?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: Series of carrier-based multirole combat aircraft.
Despite the name, this pseudocereal isn't related to true cereals at all — it's kin to rhubarb and sorrel, and was first cultivated in Yunnan around 6,000 BC — which crop is it?
Buckwheat: Species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
This suborder of 'dog-like' carnivores includes bears, raccoons, weasels, and seals, and is thought to have diversified mainly across North America and northern Eurasia — what's it called?
Caniformia: Suborder of mammals. Caniformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "dog-like" carnivorans.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine, this class of molecules includes adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine, and drives the fight-or-flight response when released from the adrenal glands. What are they called?
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)

This small, ground-nesting game bird has a call of three quick chirps repeated in succession, breeds across Europe, and winters in Africa and southern India — which species, often confused with a similar-sounding Japanese cousin?
Common quail: Species of bird. The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.
This interdisciplinary field draws on sociology, psychology, and law to study crime, deviant behavior, and the workings of the justice system — what is it called?
Criminology: Field of studies related to crimes.
At just 37 this American biologist won a 1975 Nobel for discovering reverse transcriptase, later running Caltech and founding the Whitehead Institute — who is he?
David Baltimore: American biologist and Nobel laureate (1938–2025)
These warmblooded reptiles ruled the land for the whole Mesozoic, and one feathered lineage of theirs survived the extinction 66 million years ago as today's birds — what group is this?
Dinosaur: Clade of reptiles. Since then, mounted fossil dinosaur skeletons have been major attractions at museums worldwide, and dinosaurs have become an enduring part of popular culture.
Also called a quake, tremor or temblor, it is the shaking of the surface caused by a sudden release of energy — in which layer of the Earth?
An earthquake is the shaking of the Earth's surface resulting from a sudden release of energy in the lithosphere that creates seismic waves.
Continuous with the outer nuclear membrane and absent from red blood cells, this organelle comes in rough and smooth forms and handles protein folding — what is it?
Endoplasmic reticulum: Cell organelle that processes proteins.
Recognizable by its striking yellow-and-azure plumage, this small European songbird nests in tree holes and can acrobatically hang upside-down from branch tips — which bird?
Eurasian blue tit: Species of bird. The Eurasian blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae.

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
Developed by IBM with a reference manual released in 1956, this programming language became the go-to choice for numerical weather prediction and supercomputer benchmarks — what language is it?
This field studies the relationship between food and culture, encompassing everything from cooking techniques and regional cuisines to the science of good eating — what is it called?

Gastronomy: Study of the relationship between food and culture. One who is well versed in gastronomy is called a gastronome, while a gastronomist is one who unites theory and practice in the study of gastronomy.

A colorless, sweet-tasting, syrupy liquid, this sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of triglycerides in fats and oils, and doubles as a food-industry sweetener. What is it?

Native to Africa and among the oldest of the chicken-like Galliformes birds, one domesticated species of this family wears a distinctive helmet-shaped casque and has been introduced worldwide — what are they?
Guinea fowl: Family of birds. Guinea fowl or guineafowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
Nicknamed a 'strawberry mark' in infants, this usually benign vascular tumor tends to grow for about a year before gradually shrinking — what is it?
Hemangioma: Vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Ashy-grey with a black head, throat and wings, this corvid was split into its own species in 2002 only to be folded back into its all-black relative by a 2025 reclassification — name the bird?
Hooded crow: Species of bird. The hooded crow (Corvus corone cornix), also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow (Corvus corone) in the genus Corvus.

Defined as a blood sodium level below 135 millimoles per liter, this condition can arise from drinking excessive water — or even too much beer — and in severe cases causes seizures or coma — what is it?
Hyponatremia: Low sodium concentration in the blood.
Discovered by Bernard Courtois in 1811, this heaviest stable halogen melts to a deep violet liquid and is the heaviest essential nutrient — needed to make thyroid hormones. What element is it?
Iodine: Chemical element with atomic number 53 (I)
Serving as special adviser to the UN Secretary-General from 2002 to 2018, which Columbia University economist co-founded a nonprofit dedicated to ending extreme poverty?
This twin-engine fighter jet program made its home nation the fourth in the world to develop stealth avionics, joining the ranks of the US, China, and Russia — which aircraft?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: South Korean fighter aircraft.
Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine, this spicy Southeast Asian noodle dish is often served in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind — what is it?
Laksa: Spicy noodle dish from Southeast Asia.
This genus of bulb-grown flowering plants, prized for their large blooms, is highly toxic to cats — even though many unrelated plants borrow its common name — which genus?
Lilium: Genus of plants. Lilium ( LIL-ee-əm) is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Oblate rather than round, with a thin, loose peel that makes it easy to separate into segments, this citrus fruit is sweeter and stronger-tasting than its spherical, hybrid cousin — which fruit?
Mandarin orange: Small citrus fruit. A mandarin orange (Citrus reticulata), often simply called mandarin, is a small, rounded citrus tree fruit.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
This branch of economics studies how individual firms and consumers allocate scarce resources, as opposed to the economy-wide view of its counterpart — which field?
Microeconomics: Behavior of individuals and firms.
Known as simple sugars, these colorless, water-soluble crystalline compounds include glucose and fructose and serve as the building blocks of starch and cellulose — what are they called?
Monosaccharide: Simple sugars such as glucose and fructose.

First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, this genus in the family Myrtaceae includes only two accepted species today: one native to the Mediterranean, the other to the Saharan mountains of North Africa — which genus?
Myrtus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
This small sauropod dinosaur had a wide muzzle packed with more than 500 teeth that were replaced roughly every two weeks — what genus is it?

This family of 138 primate species — including baboons, macaques, and mandrills — split off from a separate lineage of primates some 45 to 55 million years ago, yet is the closer kin to apes of the two — which family?
Old World monkey: Family of mammals. Old World monkey genera include baboons (genus Papio), red colobus (genus Piliocolobus), and macaques (genus Macaca).
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.
An adult female of this ruminant is a ewe, a castrated male a wether, and a young one a lamb — and with about 1.2 billion of them, they're easily the most common of their kind. What animal?
Sheep: Domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.

Allowing one neuron to send signals to a neighboring cell, this junction can be chemical or electrical, with coupled electrical types creating synchronized brain activity via gap junctions — what is it?
Synapse: Structure connecting neurons in the nervous system.
Also called lockjaw, this bacterial infection from Clostridium tetani starts spasms in the jaw before spreading body-wide, sometimes hard enough to fracture bone — what is it?
Tetanus: Bacterial infection characterized by muscle spasms.
Named from the Latin word for 'to ring,' this common condition causes people to perceive sounds — often ringing — that no one else can hear. What is it called?
Also called the jigger or chigoe flea, this burrowing parasite causes an infestation known as tungiasis and is often mistaken for an unrelated mite — which species?
Tunga penetrans: Species of flea. It is a parasitic insect found in most tropical and sub-tropical climates.
Caused by white blood cells migrating into and damaging vessel walls, this group of disorders inflames both arteries and veins, and sometimes even the lymphatic vessels — what condition is it?
Vasculitis: Medical disorders that destroy blood vessels by inflammation.
With a heart-shaped white facial disc and an eerie screech instead of a hoot, this nocturnal hunter locates small mammals purely by sound — which bird?
Western barn owl: Species of owl. The western barn owl (Tyto alba) is a species of barn owl native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and Africa.

Known for quoting multiple religious scriptures in English lectures delivered in a suit and tie rather than traditional robes, this Indian preacher had his foundation banned in 2016 amid hate-speech and money-laundering accusations. Who is he?
